key_insight: Longer visual history only helps robot control when the underlying video model is pretrained autoregressively (AR). Long-WAM shows that careful model-system design can extend context length without breaking real-time action.
problem_solved: Real-time robot control needs enough past visual context to understand motion and task progress, but processing long histories can introduce latency and slow action decisions.
method: Build a model-system framework for causal world-action models that can use longer context while staying within real-time control limits.
Pretrain the video foundation autoregressively so the model learns to better exploit extended visual history.
Learn causal prediction from robot and egocentric video data, then evaluate how context length affects control performance under latency constraints.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners in robotics, this work shows that scaling context is not just an engineering issue—it depends on how the backbone is pretrained. It provides a practical path toward more temporally aware robot policies without sacrificing responsiveness.

paper_title: Long-WAM: Scaling the Context of World-Action Models
paper_authors: Wei Huang, Bohan Zhang, Chenzhi Liu, Isabella Liu, Shuai Yang
